# PingOne

## Single sign-on (SAML 2.0)

In the portal, choose **PingOne** under Enterprise SSO and **Start with PingOne**. Then, in PingOne:

1. In the PingOne admin console, go to Applications → Applications and click the + icon.
2. Enter an Application Name, choose the SAML application type, and click Configure.
3. Choose Import from URL with our metadata URL below, or Manually Enter the ACS URLs and Entity ID, then Save.
4. On the Configuration tab, set Subject NameID format to urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress and map Email Address to the subject on Attribute Mappings.
5. Turn the application on, then copy the IDP Metadata URL from the Overview tab.

### The values the portal shows

| PingOne field | Value |
|---|---|
| Import from URL, optional | The portal's SP metadata URL (`https://…/sso/saml/…/metadata`) |
| ACS URLs | The portal's ACS URL (`https://…/sso/saml/…/acs`) |
| Entity ID | The portal's entity ID (`https://…/sso/saml/…`) |
| Subject NameID format (Configuration) | `urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress` |
| SLO Endpoint (Configuration), optional | The portal's Single Logout URL (`https://…/sso/saml/…/slo`) |

### What to bring back

Copy **IDP Metadata URL** — the URL, or the XML — and paste it into the portal's **Metadata URL or XML**. Prefer the URL.

The assertion must be signed, and must carry the person's email address as an attribute or as a NameID in the `emailAddress` format. See [Any SAML 2.0 provider](generic-saml.md) for the details.

PingOne's own guide: <https://docs.pingidentity.com/pingone/applications/p1_applications_add_applications.html>.

Then verify your domain and turn single sign-on on in the portal: [Enterprise SSO](../sso.md).

## Directory Sync (SCIM)

In the portal, choose **PingOne** under Directory sync and **Create directory**; copy the bearer token now, it is shown once. Then, in PingOne:

1. Go to Integrations → Provisioning, click + and New Connection, then select Identity Store and the SCIM Outbound tile.
2. Enter the SCIM Base URL below, set Authentication Method to OAuth 2 Bearer Token, paste the token below into OAuth Access Token, set Auth Type Header to Bearer, and click Test connection.
3. Choose the user actions to allow, save, and turn the connection on.
4. Click + and New Rule, choose PingOne as Source, select this connection and set the user filter and groups.

### The values the portal shows

| PingOne field | Value |
|---|---|
| SCIM Base URL | The portal's SCIM base URL (`https://…/scim/v2`) |
| Authentication Method | `OAuth 2 Bearer Token` |
| OAuth Access Token | The bearer token the portal shows once |
| Auth Type Header | `Bearer` |

PingOne's own guide: <https://docs.pingidentity.com/pingone/integrations/p1_create_scim_connection.html>.
